title: A principal-quotient criterion for an analytically unramified local domain
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $0\ne t\in\mathfrak m$. An associated prime of the $A$-module $A/tA$ is a prime ideal equal to the annihilator of a nonzero class in $A/tA$. Suppose $A/tA$ has no embedded associated primes: each associated prime is minimal among primes containing $tA$. Suppose for every associated prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A/tA$ that the local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], and that $A/\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified], i.e. its completion at $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$ is reduced. Then $A$ is analytically unramified: its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion is reduced.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0330 (lemma-criterion-analytically-unramified), lines 45917-45962; tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Let $\widehat A=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It is a Noetherian ring by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]; in particular the image of $t\in\mathfrak m$ lies in $\mathfrak m\widehat A$. The canonical map $A\to\widehat A$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. Since $A$ is a domain and $t\neq0$, multiplication by $t$ is an injective $A$-linear map $A\to A$; tensoring it with the flat $A$-module $\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] gives that multiplication by $t$ on $A\otimes_A\widehat A=\widehat A$ is injective, i.e. $t$ is a nonzerodivisor of $\widehat A$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0330 (lemma-criterion-analytically-unramified), lines 45934-45962: 'Since x is a nonzerodivisor (as R -> R^ is flat)', with Lemma 00MB (lemma-completion-flat) and Lemma 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian)

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p$ be an associated prime of $A/tA$, say $\mathfrak p=\operatorname{Ann}_A(\bar z)$. Since $t$ kills $A/tA$, $t\in\mathfrak p$, and by the hypothesis of no embedded primes $\mathfrak p$ is minimal among primes containing $tA$. Height at most one: apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with one element $f_1=t$, $J=tA$, $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak p$: $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p/tA)+1$, and $\mathfrak p/tA$ is a minimal prime of $A/tA$ (primes of $A/tA$ are the primes of $A$ containing $tA$), so it has height $0$; thus $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\le1$. Height at least one: $A$ is a domain, so $(0)$ is a prime, and $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ since $0\neq t\in\mathfrak p$. Hence $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)=1$, and $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)=1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]. The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. In Lean use the direct principal-ideal height bound Ideal.height_le_one_of_isPrincipal_of_mem_minimalPrimes, and the lower bound Ideal.one_le_height_span_singleton_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors followed by Ideal.height_mono; these specialize the height argument without constructing the prime in a quotient.

proof.text: For every associated prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A/tA$ and every associated prime $\mathfrak q$ of the $\widehat A$-module $\widehat A/\mathfrak p\widehat A$, the localization $\widehat A_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring, in particular an integral domain: apply [lem-weil-pbc-codimension-one-analytically-unramified] to the Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and the prime $\mathfrak p$, whose hypotheses are Step 3 ($A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a DVR) and the hypothesis that $\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified].

proof.text: Use associatedPrimes_quotient_map_of_flat [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-flat-quotient], with R=A, S=the maximal-ideal-adic completion and I=span{t}. Flatness is AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian. Ideal.map_span identifies the extended principal ideal with span of the image of t. Each associated prime Q of the completed principal quotient therefore belongs to Ass(S/pS) for some associated prime p of A/tA. The completion is Noetherian by Step 1, so isAssociatedPrime_iff supplies the exact annihilator witness needed by Step 4. Applying Step 4 gives that S_Q is a domain.

proof.text: Let $y\in\widehat A$ with $y^2=0$. Then $y=ty'$ for some $y'\in\widehat A$ with $y'^2=0$. Proof: for each associated prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $\widehat A/t\widehat A$ the image $y/1$ of $y$ in the domain $\widehat A_{\mathfrak Q}$ (Step 5) satisfies $(y/1)^2=0$, so $y/1=0$, i.e. $sy=0$ for some $s\in\widehat A\setminus\mathfrak Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; then also $s\bar y=0$ for the class $\bar y$ of $y$ in $\widehat A/t\widehat A$, so $\bar y/1=0$ in $(\widehat A/t\widehat A)_{\mathfrak Q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. As $\widehat A$ is Noetherian (Step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] applied to the $\widehat A$-module $\widehat A/t\widehat A$ gives $\bar y=0$, i.e. $y=ty'$ with $y'\in\widehat A$. Then $t^2y'^2=y^2=0$, and since $t$ is a nonzerodivisor of $\widehat A$ (Step 1), $y'^2=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0330 (lemma-criterion-analytically-unramified), lines 45934-45962: 'Let y in R^ with y^2 = 0 ... y maps to zero in (R^)_{q_ij}. Hence y maps to zero in R^/xR^ by Lemma lemma-zero-at-ass-zero. Hence y = xy'. Since x is a nonzerodivisor ... (y')^2 = 0' (Lemma Tag 0311)

proof.text: Every $y\in\widehat A$ with $y^2=0$ is $0$. By induction on $n\ge0$ we show the claim $C(n)$: every $y\in\widehat A$ with $y^2=0$ lies in $t^n\widehat A$. $C(0)$ is trivial. Assume $C(n)$ and let $y^2=0$; by Step 6 $y=ty'$ with $y'^2=0$, by $C(n)$ $y'\in t^n\widehat A$, so $y\in t^{n+1}\widehat A$; this is $C(n+1)$. Hence $y\in\bigcap_{n\ge0}t^n\widehat A=\bigcap_{n\ge0}(t\widehat A)^n\widehat A$. The ideal $t\widehat A$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ of the local ring $\widehat A$ (Step 1), which is its Jacobson radical; $\widehat A$ is Noetherian and finitely generated as a module over itself. So [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] (with $R=M=\widehat A$, $I=t\widehat A$) gives $\bigcap_n(t\widehat A)^n\widehat A=0$, and $y=0$. The Lean proof uses Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing, the local-ring form of the cited Jacobson-radical theorem.

proof.text: $\widehat A$ is reduced, so $A$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified]. Let $z\in\widehat A$ be nilpotent and let $n\ge1$ be least with $z^n=0$. If $n\ge2$, put $w=z^{n-1}$; then $w^2=z^{2n-2}=0$ because $2n-2\ge n$, so $w=0$ by Step 7, contradicting the minimality of $n$. Hence $n=1$ and $z=0$. In Lean isReduced_iff_pow_one_lt 2 supplies this elementary nilpotent-to-square-zero reduction.
